target_customer: Offices and companies that buy employee lunches, snacks and catering
problem: Ordering and managing office meals was a time sink for companies, started when the founder had to organize lunch at Justin.tv.
business_model: service fee on catered meals plus snacks and managed cafe programs

founders.name: Arram Sabeti
founders.background_notes: Early Justin.tv employee who ordered office lunch; a talk about the company is titled as a solo non technical founder

technical_complexity.rationale: Started as a spreadsheet matching offices and restaurants; the hard part was operations and logistics, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Vendor networks and recurring office accounts help, but catering marketplaces and contract caterers could replicate the service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Contract caterers kept operating; no source shows one copying or buying Zerocater by 2023.

market_need_then: Founder described lunch duty at Justin.tv as his most frustrating job, and by May 2018 the company reported over 250 million dollars in sales on 5.6 million dollars of outside capital, which shows durable demand.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder described the company as Pandora for food in press coverage; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name and brand origin not explained in any source found. The company is known mainly in tech office circles and shares a near name with ezCater.

pivots.to: wider geographic footprint with snacks, kitchens and later cafe programs
pivots.why: National expansion per the 2018 round announcement

outcome_analysis: Zerocater grew a spreadsheet lunch ordering service into a national office food business, reaching over 250 million dollars in cumulative sales by 2018 on little outside capital and raising a 12 million dollar Series B in 2018 and 15 million dollar Series C in 2023. It is still active with about 140 people. Competition from ezCater, Fooda and contract caterers kept it from dominating, and no exit has been reported.
notes: Outside capital before the Series B was 5.6 million dollars in several earlier rounds not itemized by sources found (a 2011 equity round appears on startupintros without a verified amount). Totals of 33 to 38 million dollars seen on aggregators are unverified. Competition circa 2011 was not found in dated sources; Zesty, Eat Club, Cater2Me and ezCater appear only in later coverage. Founding year differs by source (2008 or 2009).
